text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Jordan and Egypt agree on saving the peace process and strengthening economic integration as a way of arriving at an Arab common market. President Hosni Mubarak and King Hussein exchange views by telephone on Arab developments and the peace process crisis. Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says that Jordan's attendance of the Middle East economic conference is conditional on its benefit for Arabs.

Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says Arab investment in Arab countries is a step toward a common Arab market. Four agreements were signed between Jordan and Egypt, foremost among them tying electricity networks between the two countries.
- Saudi chief of staff General Saleh bin Ali al-Muhayya on a visit to Egypt says there will soon be joint naval exercises between the two countries.

- Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation Youssef Wali agrees on recommendations to facilitate nationals with the building of houses in villages and cities to solve the housing problem in the Egyptian countryside.
- Severe hot weather helps spark a huge fire in heavy lifting machinery at Port Said.
